tax.text: Income taxes for the interim periods presented have been included in the accompanying consolidated financial statements on the basis of an estimated annual effective tax rate. The determination of the consolidated provision for income taxes requires management to make certain judgments and estimates. Changes in the estimated level of annual pre-tax earnings, tax laws, and changes resulting from tax audits can affect the overall effective income tax rate, which impacts the level of income tax expense and net income. Judgments and estimates related to the company’s projections and assumptions are inherently uncertain, therefore, actual results could differ from projections.

net.text: In addition to disclosing financial results that are determined in accordance with GAAP, the company also discloses certain non-GAAP financial information in the sections below captioned “Sales by Reportable Segment,” “Gross Profit,” “Operating Expenses,” “Operating Income,” “Income Tax,” and “Net Income Attributable to Shareholders.” Refer to these sections below for reconciliations of non-GAAP financial measures to the most directly comparable reported GAAP financial measures. Non-GAAP financial information includes the following:

ocf.heading: Cash Flows from Operating Activities
ocf.text: The net amount of cash provided by the company’s operating activities during the first six months of 2026 and 2025 was $1.0 billion and $145.8 million, respectively. The change in cash provided by operating activities during 2026, compared to the year-earlier period, relates primarily to timing of settlements, most notably within the Global Components supply chain services offerings, and increase in income from operations, partially offset by higher inventory purchases to support future sales growth . The fluctuations in both “Accounts receivable, net” and “Accounts payable” are primarily related to the Global Components supply chain services offerings and are typically correlated as the company acts as an intermediary in the transaction and remits payments to the supplier upon receipt from the customer. Refer to Note E “Accounts Receivable” of the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements.

sbc.text: During the first six months of 2026, compared to the year-earlier period, corporate operating expenses also increased due to an increase in restructuring, integration and other charges (see discussion below), partially offset by timing of stock-based compensation expense mainly due to certain awards granted in the current year.

wc.heading: Working Capital
wc.text: The company maintains a significant investment in working capital, which the company defines as accounts receivable, net, plus inventories less accounts payable. The decrease in working capital during the first six months of 2026 was primarily attributable to the timing of settlements, most notably within the Global Components supply chain services offerings. Refer to Note E “Accounts Receivable” of the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements. The decrease in working capital is partially offset by higher inventory purchases to support future sales growth.

capex.heading: Capital Expenditures
capex.text: Capital expenditures for the first six months of 2026 and 2025 were $53.2 million and $43.6 million, respectively, and the company expects capital expenditures to be approximately $100.0 million for fiscal year 2026. The company's capital expenditures primarily relate to enhancements in internally developed software, mainly ArrowSphere, the company's marketplace and management platform, as well as improvements of the company's facilities and warehouses. Refer to discussion of the company’s policy on software development costs in Note 1 “Summary of Significant Accounting Policies” in the company’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025.

ocf.heading: Cash Flows from Operating Activities
ocf.text: The net amount of cash provided by the company’s operating activities during the first nine months of 2026 was $576.7 million, and the cash used for operating activities during the first nine months of 2025 was $135.9 million. The change in cash provided by operating activities during 2026, compared to the year-earlier period, relates primarily to timing of settlements, most notably within the Global Components supply chain services offerings, and increase in income from operations, partially offset by higher inventory purchases to support future sales demand . The fluctuations in both “Accounts receivable, net” and “Accounts payable” are primarily related to the Global Components supply chain services offerings and are typically correlated as the company acts as an intermediary in the transaction and remits payments to the supplier upon receipt from the customer. Refer to Note E “Accounts Receivable” of the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements.

wc.heading: Working Capital
wc.text: The company maintains a significant investment in working capital, which the company defines as accounts receivable, net, plus inventories less accounts payable. The increase in working capital during the first nine months of 2026 was primarily attributable to the higher inventory purchases to support future sales demand partially offset by timing of settlements, most notably within the Global Components supply chain services offerings. Refer to Note E “Accounts Receivable” of the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements.

capex.heading: Capital Expenditures
capex.text: Capital expenditures for the first nine months of 2026 and 2025 were $80.1 million and $73.9 million, respectively, and the company expects capital expenditures to be approximately $100.0 million for fiscal year 2026. The company's capital expenditures primarily relate to enhancements in internally developed software, mainly ArrowSphere, the company's AI-enabled marketplace and management platform, as well as improvements of the company's facilities and warehouses. Refer to discussion of the company’s policy on software development costs in Note 1 “Summary of Significant Accounting Policies” in the company’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025.

intro.text: Arrow Electronics, Inc. (the “company” or “Arrow”) sources and engineers technology for thousands of leading manufacturers, service providers, and users of enterprise computing solutions. The company has one of the world’s broadest portfolios of product offerings available from leading electronic components and enterprise computing solutions suppliers. Equipped with a range of services, solutions, and software, the company helps industrial and commercial customers introduce innovative products, reduce their time to market, and enhance their overall competitiveness. Arrow was incorporated in New York in 1946.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Income taxes payable, non-current
lines.why: Taxes on operating income due after a year (often uncertain tax positions): operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
